The question

Could moderating unusually rapid amplification improve information ecosystems while preserving access and user agency?

Full publication title

Vital Network Science: A Control-Theoretic Framework for Information Ecosystem Governance

OverviewVisual explanationSelected pagesFull paper
Overview

Governing the pace of amplification.

This companion preprint asks whether moderating the speed of online amplification could improve the health of an information ecosystem while preserving access. It proposes a seven part vitality index covering coherence, resilience, civility, epistemic quality, diversity, agency and affective balance. A proposed feedback governor would respond to unusually fast spread with temporary delays, added context, changes to recommendations or controlled throttling. The paper also sketches transparency, user override, appeal and public oversight mechanisms. Its three phase validation plan describes how the framework might be tested before wider deployment. The index, governor and governance arrangements are conceptual. The claimed benefits and numerical success targets are predictions and design goals; the paper does not report a large scale trial.

Key terms, in plain English
Vitality index
A proposed composite of coherence, resilience, civility, epistemic quality, diversity, agency and affective balance.
Feedback governor
A control mechanism that adjusts an intervention in response to observations of the system.

What the paper proposes

  • Defines a proposed vitality index across seven dimensions of information ecosystem health.
  • Describes a feedback governor that would temporarily moderate rapid amplification.
  • Sets out transparency, appeals, oversight and a phased empirical validation plan.

Research status

The paper presents a theoretical framework without large scale validation. Its vitality measurements require operational definitions and calibration. Proposed intervention times, thresholds and trial success criteria are design targets, while expected benefits remain unmeasured. The paper identifies possible governance capture, chilling effects, displacement to unregulated platforms and cultural mismatch as risks requiring further study.
